title: Laravel Blueprint
description: Schema for Blueprint draft.yaml files (https://github.com/laravel-shift/blueprint), validated against Blueprint v2.13.0. Blueprint's per-column and per-statement values use a small DSL that is not fully expressible in JSON Schema; those values are typed as free-form strings with descriptions/examples rather than strict patterns, so this schema will not catch every mistake (e.g. a misspelled column type). It focuses on catching structural mistakes: unknown top-level sections, unknown model/controller/meta keys, and unknown statement names. Note: Blueprint also accepts bare-word shorthand with no value on its own line (e.g. `softDeletes`, `id`, `timestamps`, `resource`, `invokable`, `uuid`, `ulid`) that it rewrites before YAML is even parsed — that form isn't valid standard YAML and can't be represented here; use the explicit `key: true` / `resource: web` form shown in this schema instead. `components:` (Livewire) is intentionally not covered, as it isn't wired into the released build pipeline yet.

models.description: Eloquent models to generate, keyed by class name. Nest under a subdirectory with `/` or `\` (e.g. `Admin/User`).

controllers.description: Controllers to generate, keyed by class name. Nest under a subdirectory with `/` or `\` (e.g. `Admin/User`).

seeders.description: Comma-separated list of model names to generate a DatabaseSeeder call for.

config.description: Overrides Blueprint's own config/blueprint.php for this build only. Unlisted keys are still allowed since custom Generator classes may read their own config values.

models_namespace.description: Defaults to `Models`. Set to `null` to generate directly under the root namespace.

use_constraints.description: Add foreign key constraints to generated migrations.

model.description: A model definition. Special keys configure the primary key, timestamps, soft deletes, relationships, indexes, and class-level metadata; every other key is a column name.

id.description: Primary key column. Omitted/`true` uses the default `id bigIncrements` column; `false` disables the primary key entirely; or provide a column definition to customize it (e.g. `uuid primary`, `increments`).

timestampstz.description: Alias of `timestampsTz`; key matching is case-insensitive.

softDeletes.description: Add a deleted_at column and the SoftDeletes trait.

softdeletes.description: Alias of `softDeletes`; key matching is case-insensitive.

softdeletestz.description: Alias of `softDeletesTz`; key matching is case-insensitive.

meta.description: Class-level model configuration. (If you have a genuine column named `meta`, give it a column definition string instead and Blueprint will treat it as a column.)

indexes.description: Composite/custom indexes beyond what column modifiers (unique, index, primary) already declare inline.

connection.description: Database connection name this model should use.

table.description: Override the default (snake_case, plural) table name.

pivot.description: Mark this model as a pivot model for a belongsToMany relationship.

extends.description: Fully-qualified class name to extend instead of Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model.

traits.description: Comma-separated list of fully-qualified trait names to `use`.

implements.description: Comma-separated list of fully-qualified interface names to implement.

relationships.description: Eloquent relationships this model defines. Each value is one model reference, or a comma-separated list of them. A reference may include a namespace (`\App\Models\Team`), a custom foreign key alias (`Model:column`), or for belongsToMany/morphToMany, a custom pivot model (`Model:&PivotModel`). For hasOneThrough/hasManyThrough, the reference is `Target:Intermediate`. Relationship type keys are matched case-insensitively by Blueprint; the canonical camelCase spellings are listed here for autocomplete, but other casings are also accepted.

throughRelationshipValue.description: One `Target:Intermediate` model reference, or a comma-separated list of them.

index.description: A single index. The key is the Schema Blueprint method to call (commonly `unique`, `index`, `primary`, or `fullText`); the value is one column name or a comma-separated list.

columnDefinition.description:
`<type>[:attribute,...] [modifier[:value]]...`

Types: bigIncrements, bigInteger, binary, boolean, char, date, dateTime, dateTimeTz, decimal, double, enum, float, fullText, geography, geometry, geometryCollection, id, increments, integer, ipAddress, json, jsonb, lineString, longText, macAddress, mediumIncrements, mediumInteger, mediumText, morphs, uuidMorphs, multiLineString, multiPoint, multiPolygon, nullableMorphs, nullableUuidMorphs, nullableTimestamps, point, polygon, rememberToken, set, smallIncrements, smallInteger, softDeletes, softDeletesTz, string, text, time, timeTz, timestamp, timestampTz, timestamps, timestampsTz, tinyIncrements, tinyInteger, unsignedBigInteger, unsignedDecimal, unsignedInteger, unsignedMediumInteger, unsignedSmallInteger, unsignedTinyInteger, ulid, uuid, year. (Type is optional; omitting it with only `foreign` infers `id`.)

Modifiers: autoIncrement, charset:value, collation:value, default:value, nullable, unsigned, useCurrent, useCurrentOnUpdate, always, unique, index, primary, foreign[:table[.column]], onDelete[:cascade|restrict|no_action|null], onUpdate[:...], comment:value.

Type and modifiers are space-separated; type attributes are comma-separated after a colon.

controller.description: A controller definition. `resource` generates standard CRUD methods, `invokable` generates a single-action controller, `meta` configures class-level options, and any other key is a custom action method.

resource.description: Generate resource methods: `true`/`web` for the 7 standard web actions, `api` for the 5 API actions, or a comma-separated subset of action names (index, create, store, show, edit, update, destroy, or api.index/api.store/api.show/api.update/api.destroy).

invokable.description: Generate a single-action (`__invoke`) controller. `true` renders a default view named after the model, or provide statements directly.

policies.description: Generate and apply a policy. `true` authorizes the full standard resource ability map; or a comma-separated list of actions (index, show, create, store, edit, update, destroy) to limit which abilities are checked.

parent.description: The model this controller acts on, when it can't be inferred from the controller's name.

store.description: A relationship path to save/query through, e.g. `user.posts`.

extends.description: Fully-qualified class name to extend instead of the app's base controller.

traits.description: Comma-separated list of fully-qualified trait names to `use`.

implements.description: Comma-separated list of fully-qualified interface names to implement.

controllerStatements.description: One or more statements to generate within a controller action, keyed by statement name. Repeat a statement (e.g. two `fire` events in one action) by suffixing a unique label after a dash, e.g. `fire-welcome`, `dispatch-1`.

respond.description: A view/resource name, or a bare HTTP status code (e.g. `204`).

statementValue.description: Most statements follow `<subject> [with:field,field,...]`, e.g. `render post.show with:post` or `redirect posts.index`.
